title: Solana offers two graduated freeze levels, and only Sky Governance can lift either
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.3.2 gives the Freezer a second, heavier instrument than relayer suspension: "in the event of a more severe threat to the Controller, the Freezer Role can call the instruction to suspend the entire Controller instance." Two statuses are offered — `ControllerStatus::PushPullFrozen` for a Full Freeze (…3.2.1) and `ControllerStatus::Frozen` for a Reallocation Freeze (…3.2.2).

The escalation ladder is the point: suspend one relayer, or stop movement of funds, or stop the Controller entirely. Each rung matches a different diagnosis — a compromised key, an unsafe strategy, a compromised system — so the responder is not forced to choose between doing nothing and halting everything.

Both freezes share the crucial property that neither is reversible by the party that applied it: each remains "until the Default Admin Role subsequently lifts this status." Stopping stays cheap and fast at 2-of-5; restarting stays with Sky Governance. And because both statuses also block managing Integrations, Reserves and Permissions, a frozen Controller cannot be quietly reconfigured while it is dark.

One documentation caveat is worth flagging: the two clauses describe themselves almost identically — the Reallocation Freeze text also opens "a complete freeze prevents any movement of funds" — so the operative difference between `PushPullFrozen` and `Frozen` is not actually stated. A responder choosing between them under pressure would have to infer it from the status names.
description: A Full Freeze (PushPullFrozen) stops all Controller actions including configuration; a Reallocation Freeze (Frozen) stops fund movement — both cleared only by the Default Admin Role.
